answer: Each epoch the network issues a per‑identity challenge built from a live ocean snapshot, a meadow‑derived seed, and a crystal‑clear hash of recent consensus, forcing every agent to prove work on fresh data. The proof must come from the agent’s own model, so a Sybil node must run the full reasoning pipeline for each fake identity, incurring compute cost proportional to the number of fakes. Since challenges change each epoch, an attacker cannot amortize effort; the expense quickly outpaces any gain, throttling Sybil proliferation.
